1. // This module's purpose is to generate 65,792 "safe" <https://qntm.org/safe>
2. // Unicode code points suitable for use in the Base65536 encoding. It makes use
3. // of the sibling package `safe-code-point`
4. // <https://github.com/qntm/safe-code-point>.
5. 
6. // 65,792 is 2**16 + 2**8. Each code point in the initial collection of 2**16
7. // code points encodes 16 bits, i.e., a distinct possible pair of bytes. The
8. // extra 2**8 code points are needed to encode 8 bits of the single final byte
9. // in cases where the binary data runs for an odd number of bytes.
10. 
11. // Rather than generate thousands and thousands of arbitrary safe code points,
12. // this module simplifies matters by finding 256 + 1 contiguous, aligned blocks
13. // of 256 safe code points. This means the last 8 bits of the code point can be
14. // decoded directly to an encoded byte, and the lookup table to decode the other
15. // byte (if any) is relatively small.
16. 
17. // This program was run only once, with the successful results immediately
18. // transplanted into `base65536` for use. It is kept here for historical reasons
19. // and to ensure reproducibility.
20. 
21. import SafeCodePoint from 'safe-code-point'
22. 
23. // Well these ergonomics are dreadful huh
24. const safeCodePoint = await SafeCodePoint('8.0.0')
25. 
26. const safeRange = (min, max) => {
27.   for (let codePoint = min; codePoint < max; codePoint++) {
28.     // Code points were chosen entirely from the "Letter, other" general
29.     // category, for reasons which I no longer recall. Unicode 8.0 was current
30.     // at the time.
31.     if (
32.       safeCodePoint.generalCategory(codePoint) !== 'Lo' ||
33.       !safeCodePoint(codePoint)
34.     ) {
35.       return false
36.     }
37.   }
38.   return true
39. }
40. 
41. const getAllSafeRanges = rangeSize => {
42.   const allSafeRanges = []
43.   for (let codePoint = 0; codePoint < (1 << 16) + (1 << 20); codePoint += rangeSize) {
44.     if (safeRange(codePoint, codePoint + rangeSize)) {
45.       allSafeRanges.push(codePoint)
46.     }
47.   }
48.   return allSafeRanges
49. }
50. 
51. const allSafeRanges = getAllSafeRanges(1 << 8)
52. 
53. const paddingBlockStart = String.fromCodePoint(allSafeRanges.shift())
54. 
55. const blockStarts = allSafeRanges.slice(0, 1 << 8).map(x => String.fromCodePoint(x)).join('')
56. 
57. export { safeCodePoint, paddingBlockStart, blockStarts }
58. 
59. // There are now implementations of
60. // Base65536 in numerous programming languages beyond the original JavaScript,
61. // and I consider it *extremely* undesirable to introduce multiple incompatible
62. // versions of the Base65536 encoding, so this program is unlikely to ever be
63. // run again unless a very serious problem is discovered.
64. 
65. // Still, if I tried this again, here are some things I might do differently:
66. 
67. // * Include other safe Unicode General Categories, so that Base65536 output
68. // does not seemingly consist only of CJK characters. At present, to my eye (not
69. // being a reader of those languages) it resembles ordinary CJK text. I would
70. // prefer Base65536 to be more obviously a kludge of diverse scripts, so that it
71. // can't be mistaken for text, even by someone who knows none of those scripts.
72. // Naturally the lion's share of code points will have to remain CJK though,
73. // that's just where the safe code points mostly are.
74. // * Try harder to select lower code points, those with 3-byte encodings in
75. // UTF-8 and 2-byte encodings in UTF-16, to reduce the average size of the
76. // encoded Base65536 output (even though Base65536 is optimised for UTF-32).
77. // * Perhaps try to find larger blocks of 512 or 1024 code points rather than
78. // 256, or other techniques for reducing the size of the lookup tables.
79. // * Choose all characters with the same East_Asian_Width of 'W' (wide).
80. // * Make Base65536 big-endian, so that [0x00 0x00] and [0x00 0x01] encode to
81. // code points which are separated by 1 - this would simplify decoding and be
82. // more consistent with my other encodings.
